complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Database schema design and SQLAlchemy models implementation
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down the implementation of SQLAlchemy 2.0 models by domain. Create subtasks for: (1) Setting up Base model and common mixins (UUID, timestamps), (2) Auth domain models (User with security fields), (3) Products domain (Product, ProductCategory, PriceHistory with relationships), (4) Inventory domain (InventoryLevel, StockMovement), (5) Sales domain (DailySales with indexes), (6) Orders domain (Order, OrderItem, OrderPayment with computed fields), (7) FX domain (FXRate, FXForecast with unique constraints), (8) Cashflow domain (LoanObligation, OperatingCost, CashflowProjection), (9) Pricing domain (PricingRecommendation, PortfolioMargin), (10) AI Engine domain (Recommendation, ScenarioSimulation). Each subtask should include implementing the model with mapped_column(), relationships, __repr__ methods, and ensuring all Decimal types are used for currency.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task has high complexity (8/10) because it involves implementing 30+ models across 9 domains from scratch. Each domain has 2-4 models with complex relationships, computed properties, unique constraints, and specific SQLAlchemy 2.0 patterns using mapped_column() and Mapped[] annotations. The models require careful attention to data types (Decimal for currency, UUID for IDs, DateTime with timezone), proper indexing strategy, and relationship configuration. The codebase currently has only TODOs in all model files, so this is complete greenfield development requiring deep SQLAlchemy 2.0 knowledge.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Alembic migrations for complete database schema
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Create subtasks for Alembic migration implementation: (1) Update alembic/env.py to import all domain models for detection, (2) Generate initial migration using alembic revision --autogenerate, (3) Review and enhance migration file - add explicit indexes for frequently queried columns (User.email, Product.sku, DailySales.sale_date, Order.order_date, FXRate.rate_date), (4) Add composite indexes for multi-column queries (DailySales on product_id+sale_date, FXForecast on currency_pair+target_date), (5) Test migration application (upgrade head) and verify all tables, columns, and constraints exist using SQLAlchemy inspect(), (6) Test migration reversibility (downgrade -1, upgrade head) and document common commands in alembic/README.md.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity (5/10) because the Alembic configuration is already set up for async operations. The main work involves ensuring all models are imported, reviewing autogenerated migrations, adding explicit indexes for performance, and thorough testing. The task is dependent on Task 1 being complete. While conceptually straightforward, it requires careful attention to index strategy and constraint validation to ensure the schema matches the complex domain model requirements.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down authentication implementation into: (1) Implement password hashing utilities using passlib with bcrypt in service.py, (2) Implement create_user() with password validation (12+ chars, complexity requirements), (3) Implement authenticate_user() with failed login tracking and 15-minute lockout logic, (4) Implement JWT token creation and validation using python-jose with 24-hour expiration, (5) Create auth dependencies (get_current_user, get_current_active_user) for route protection, (6) Implement all auth router endpoints (POST /register, /login, /logout, GET /me), (7) Set up Redis token blacklist for logout functionality, (8) Implement rate limiting (100 req/min per session) using Redis. complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity (7/10) due to multiple security considerations: password hashing with bcrypt, JWT token management, failed login tracking with lockout mechanism, rate limiting using Redis, and token blacklisting. The implementation requires careful handling of security edge cases, proper async operations, and integration with Redis for rate limiting and token blacklisting. All service and router files currently contain only TODOs. The task involves creating a production-ready authentication system with comprehensive security features as specified in the PRD.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Daily sales entry with automatic inventory updates
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down sales implementation: (1) Implement create_daily_sales_entry() with atomic transaction handling (DailySales + inventory update + StockMovement), (2) Add overselling prevention using SELECT FOR UPDATE on inventory rows, (3) Implement get_sales_by_date_range() with efficient queries, (4) Implement get_sales_velocity() using SQLAlchemy window functions for 30-day rolling average, (5) Implement get_sales_summary() with aggregate queries by product/date, (6) Implement update_sales_entry() that correctly adjusts inventory delta, (7) Implement delete_sales_entry() with inventory reversal and audit logging, (8) Implement bulk_upload_sales_csv() with CSV parsing, validation, and batch transaction processing, (9) Add all router endpoints with proper error handling for insufficient stock (400), CSV validation errors (422), and transaction rollback on failures.

Key challenges: preventing overselling with SELECT FOR UPDATE locks, handling concurrent sales entries without race conditions, CSV bulk upload with line-by-line validation and error reporting, sales velocity calculation for demand forecasting, and ensuring inventory adjustments are always reversible. The service file is currently empty (TODOs only). This task is critical for data integrity as sales directly affect inventory levels, and errors could lead to inventory discrepancies.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: FX forecasting engine with Prophet and Monte Carlo simulation
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down FX forecasting implementation: (1) Implement train_fx_forecast_model() - fetch 180 days historical data, prepare Prophet format {ds, y}, (2) Configure Prophet with multiplicative seasonality and fit model, (3) Save trained model to disk with versioning and log MAE metrics, (4) Implement generate_fx_forecast() - load model, generate 180-day forecast, (5) Implement Monte Carlo simulation using NumPy - 10,000 runs per forecast date with normal distribution (mean=Prophet forecast, std=historical volatility), (6) Calculate percentiles (5th=best case, 50th=base, 95th=worst case) and store in FXForecast table, (7) Implement get_forecast_for_date() with staleness check (regenerate if >7 days old), (8) Implement get_forecast_range() for time series retrieval, (9) Implement update_forecast_accuracy() comparing past forecasts to actuals (MAE, MAPE), (10) Wrap Prophet operations in thread pool executor for async compatibility. Include comprehensive tests with synthetic data and performance validation (<10s for 180-day forecast).
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Very high complexity (9/10) because this is sophisticated AI/ML work requiring Prophet time-series forecasting combined with Monte Carlo simulation for scenario generation. Key challenges: preparing data in correct Prophet format, configuring Prophet hyperparameters for FX data, running 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations efficiently using NumPy, managing model persistence with versioning, wrapping CPU-intensive Prophet operations for async compatibility, and implementing accuracy tracking for continuous model improvement. Key challenges: training Prophet models on sales time series, implementing elasticity and FX sensitivity coefficients correctly, formulating the optimization problem with proper constraints (prices > cost * 1.10, maintain total revenue ±5%), and creating actionable recommendations that balance individual product margins with portfolio-level targets.
